runtime_status: runtime-evidenced on Windows PowerShell 5.1: every MCP server in three live provider configs completed a real initialize -> tools/list exchange, and the three dead command paths found there were repaired and re-verified. Linux/static/artifact gates pass in CI.
notes: v7.9.5: capability profiles. Seven MCP servers evaluated from an external capability review are shipped as named profiles in BUNDLED-TOOLS/PROFILES.json rather than registered globally -- Serena, Chrome DevTools, shadcn, Supabase, Blender, Godot and Unity. The reason is measurable: TOOLS/Test-McpHandshake.ps1 ran the real initialize -> tools/list exchange against this machine's live configs and found 188 tool schemas riding in context on every turn of every Claude session, against 136 for Codex and 90 for Grok. Skills are lazy and MCP schemas are not, so the profile router wires a server only when the project shows its markers and the machine satisfies its requirements, and prints the missing prerequisite otherwise instead of writing an entry that fails on first call. Both config writers now share TOOLS/V7-Mcp-Write.ps1: every config bug this pack has shipped was a bug in one of three config shapes that the other two did not have. The new gate TESTS/Test-McpProfiles.ps1 caught two on its first run -- PowerShell unrolls a single-element array on return, so a one-argument server would have been written as "args": "blender-mcp"; and -CheckOnly deleted the entries it claimed it would only report on. The handshake probe then found a live defect no static check could: Codex still held @playwright/mcp@latest with no -y, so npx blocked on an install prompt and the server never answered initialize. Update-V5GrokMcpBlock -SkipIfPresent compared only the command, and every npx server has the same command -- so a pin added in a later release could never reach a machine that already had the entry. It now compares the args. Unreal MCP was evaluated and not shipped: last upstream commit 2025-06-06. 144 canonical skills across 5 provider trees. Pointing the probe at live configs after CI was green produced five more fixes that no static check could reach: CATALOG.json's own Playwright entry had no -y (widening the contract from the new servers to every npx entry then caught firecrawl-mcp and @perplexity-ai/mcp-server unpinned, now 3.24.0 and 1.2.0 against the npm registry); the probe redirected stderr and never drained it, so a chatty server blocked on a full pipe and was reported as a false FAIL; the profile router double-registered on Grok, which reads ~/.claude.json as well as its own config; and Repair-McpPaths.ps1 could not repoint Codex's hash-named runtime directories because its rule assumed a version-stamped sibling -- generalised to 'exactly one sibling under which the tail exists', with two candidates still reported rather than guessed between. Live handshakes afterwards: Claude 9/9 (211 tool schemas per turn), Codex 11/11 (235), Grok 5/5 (90). Teaching the probe Hermes' config shape then found the same unpinned Playwright there and traced it to the installer: CATALOG.json lists Hermes and Kimi as providers for three npx extras, but the npx branch only wrote Grok, Codex and Claude and printed the block at the other two -- a component the catalog claimed for five providers reached three. Both are wired through the shared writer now. The helper-existence gate was hardcoded to one shared module and now collects from every one. Hermes handshake: 10/10 (240 tool schemas per turn).
